newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Schiphol Feb air cargo hit by lower KLM volume.
newsitem.headline: Schiphol Feb air cargo hit by lower KLM volume.

text.p: Lower February air cargo traffic at Schiphol was mainly a reflection of less airfreight carried by KLM Royal Dutch Airlines NV, an airport spokeswoman told Reuters.
Another factor was that February this year was one day shorter than last year, a leap year and that in 1996 the month was exceptionally good, she added.
February's total freight throughput at Schiphol was 86,919 tonnes, an increase of only 0.2 pct on this time last year.
KLM spokesman Peter Wellhuner, added that the airline's airfreight traffic was down 4 pct in February compared to 1996..
He said: "In February last year we logged 300.8 million tonne kilometres, against 287.9 million tonne kilometres this year."
"Our cargo traffic in February was lower overall, specifically on routes to North America and the Middle East and Southern Asia.
Wellhuner said a new efficiency programme is now contributing to improved use of the existing KLM fleet. -- Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542-7706 Fax+5017
